title: Angstrom Lattice at a glance
intro_say: Angstrom Signals. | Angstrom Lattice, at a glance.

steps.screen: Empty diagram; the title "From signals to a scan" appears
steps.say: Every trader has their own way of reading a chart. Angstrom Lattice lets you write yours down once, | and have it checked on every asset you follow.

steps.screen: The Signals box lights up, with small icons for its six kinds
steps.say: It starts with signals: the indicators behind the dashboard, such as moving averages, RSI, volume, and market structure. Each one measures one thing.

steps.screen: An arrow to Signal Groups; a score dial from -100 to +100 and the label "Bullish"
steps.say: Signal Groups combine signals into one reading, a score from minus one hundred to plus one hundred, | with labels you choose, such as Bullish. The dashboard's already configured Trend, Stretch and Flow are Signal Groups like these.

steps.screen: An arrow to Signal Sets; two lines with ticks, then "Yes"
steps.say: Signal Sets turn readings into a decision: | Yes, No, or Unknown, | with the line that decided it. For example: the trend is bullish, | and RSI is at most forty, a pullback in an uptrend.

steps.screen: An arrow to Prism Scan; asset names fill a list, a few marked Yes
steps.say: Prism Scan runs a Set across your watchlist, | now, | at a past moment, | or on a schedule.

steps.screen: An arrow to Alerts: app, email, daily summary
steps.say: And when an asset turns Yes, you hear about it, | instantly or in your daily summary.
Strategies come next: entries, exits, and risk, built on the same Sets.

steps.screen: Quick cuts of the real screens: Signal Groups, Signal Sets, the Prism board
steps.say: Why it helps: your rules stay the same every time, | every answer shows its reasons, | and missing data is reported as Unknown, never guessed.
Everything here describes the market as it is. | It is not a forecast, and not advice.
